text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 20

The panel's composition is weak evidence on its own. All-women panels occur routinely by chance and by role (HR, senior leadership), and research doesn't show panels reliably favour their own sex. Leading with it signals grievance rather than merit and will likely harden the employer's position.

Your stronger ground is the unanswered request. Head-of-group roles weight client-facing and leadership ability heavily, and "excellent client relationships" may genuinely have outranked your extra seven years — but you're entitled to know. Send a polite written follow-up with a deadline, citing your earlier request, and ask for the scoring criteria and your assessment against them.

If the response reveals criteria invented afterwards, shifting reasons, or scoring that ignores stated requirements, then composition becomes context worth noting — not before.
